purpose: Teach: ダブル/ショット/直感/展覧/演じる/細い/逃げる/助ける

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さんと、絶対、ダブル、絶対、テニス、絶対、楽しんだぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, when we were young — you remember how seriously your father and I played doubles tennis together? Really, we did.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Warm but hesitant — searching for a shared memory across time. Gentle lift at the memory itself, then trailing into quietness. Asking to be remembered with him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、写真の、絶対、ショット、絶対、お手の物だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes. When we were young — you remember how your grandfather had such a perfect shot, didn't he? Really, he did.
lines.style: Gentle agreement, almost sighing the words. A small smile in the voice. Tender preservation of the memory, as if speaking it aloud keeps him here. Soft, sure cadence.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、直感、絶対、で、絶対、商売の、絶対、勝負所、絶対、判断したぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, your father had this instinct for business — the way he'd read a moment and make a call. You remember that, don't you, gran?
lines.style: Warmer now, pride threading through. A slight quickening on the memory of his father's decisiveness. Present tense warmth about a past person. Genuine respect in the pacing.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃんと、絶対、美術館の、絶対、展覧、絶対、会、絶対、行ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes. When we were young, your grandfather and I — we went to gallery openings together, didn't we? You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Voice brightens slightly with the memory of shared culture, shared time. Intimate, as if drawing him into a small private gallery of her own remembering. Lingering affection on the image.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、町内会の、絶対、役を、絶対、演じる、絶対、こと、絶対、よくあったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: And when we were young, your father was always playing some role in the neighborhood association — didn't he do that often, gran? You remember?
lines.style: Light wry tone — not mocking, but catching the particular earnestness of a younger man. A little laugh underneath. Still wistful, but with a thread of gentle humor running through it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃんは、絶対、細い、絶対、体つき、絶対、だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, and your grandfather — he was always so slim and lean in those days, wasn't he? Do you remember that about him?
lines.style: Matter-of-fact observation wrapped in tenderness. No judgment, just the simple seeing of a person. A slight pause, as if picturing him. Factual but suffused with love.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お孫さんが、絶対、お父さんから、絶対、逃げる、絶対、ように、絶対、隠れたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: And the grandchildren — they'd hide from your father, remember? They were always running away from him. You remember that, don't you, gran?
lines.style: A small, knowing laugh underneath. Wry affection — not unkind, but catching the comedy of a younger man's earnestness that frightened the small ones. Warmth mixed with gentle mockery.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、ご近所の方を、絶対、助ける、絶対、こと、絶対、よく、絶対、ありましたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes. Your grandfather was always helping the neighbors, wasn't he? That's what I remember — how often he'd step in when someone needed something. Don't you?
lines.style: Quiet pride in the portrait of him she's painting. Each memory placed like a small stone in a deliberate pattern. Steady, sure, spoken as if she's protecting his legacy with her own voice. Closing gentleness.
